name: Scapular Pull-Up
description: The scapular pull-up is an isolation drill performed at the top of a dead hang, where the shoulder blades are actively depressed and retracted without bending the elbows. It trains the serratus anterior, lower trapezius, and latissimus dorsi to control scapular positioning — a foundational movement for shoulder health and progression to full pull-ups.

execution.starting_position: Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip. Arms fully extended, body relaxed in a dead hang.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a bar at a height that allows full arm extension with feet off the floor. Adjust grip width to shoulder width.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a dead hang with arms fully extended.
Step 2: Without bending the elbows, actively depress and retract the shoulder blades, elevating the body 2-5 cm.
Step 3: Hold the depressed position for 1-2 seconds, feeling the lats engage.
Step 4: Slowly allow the shoulder blades to elevate back to the resting dead-hang position.
Step 5: Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you depress the scapulae. Inhale as you return to the dead hang.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — this becomes a partial pull-up rather than a scapular drill
Shrugging the traps upward instead of depressing downward
Moving too quickly — the drill is about motor control, not speed
safety_considerations: Avoid this exercise with active rotator cuff or labral injuries until cleared by a clinician
Warm up wrists and shoulders before hanging
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder blades travel from fully elevated dead hang to maximally depressed and retracted — typically 2-5 cm of body elevation.
coaching_cues: Think 'put your shoulder blades in your back pockets'
Squeeze the lats without bending the arms
